## Function that safely normalizes to logical

The PDF review dataset contains binary variables that may appear in different formats, including logical values and character encodings such as `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"true"`, `"false"`, `"1"`, and `"0"`. The `convert_to_logical()` function standardizes these inputs into `TRUE`, `FALSE`, or `NA`. This preprocessing step helps ensure that downstream comparisons between human and model-generated labels are performed on consistently formatted data.

```{r}
#| label: fn-convert-to-logical
#| eval: false
```

## Compute kappa helper

The `compute_kappa()` function calculates unweighted Cohen’s kappa for a single comparison between a human-reviewed variable and a model-generated variable. It first checks that the model variable is present in the dataset, then removes rows with missing values before calculating kappa. This helper is used when creating agreement summaries across multiple variables and models.

```{r}
#| label: fn-compute-kappa
#| eval: false
```

## Function to compute numerators, denominators, percentages

The `get_breakdown()` function creates descriptive summaries for a given human-reviewed variable by pairing it with the corresponding ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini variables. It counts positive results for each model, calculates denominators and percentages, and formats numerator/denominator strings for use in presentation tables. This function is used to build tables showing how model outputs compare with human abstraction across key study characteristics.

```{r}
#| label: fn-get-breakdown
#| eval: false
```

## Function to add readable labels for tables

The `add_label_for_gt()` function adds a `label` column to a results data frame by looking up each internal variable name in `label_list`. Variables without an entry in `label_list` keep their internal name as the label. It is used before building the kappa and breakdown `gt` tables so that rows display reader-friendly names.

```{r}
#| label: fn-add-label
#| eval: false
```

## Function to color-code kappa values

The `kappa_fill()` function maps each Cohen’s kappa value to a fill color, using bands based on the Landis and Koch agreement categories (slight, fair, moderate, substantial, almost perfect), with separate colors for negative values and exact zero. Missing kappas are left white. It is passed to `gt::data_color()` to shade the kappa tables.

```{r}
#| label: fn-kappa-fill
#| eval: false
```

## Function to create the kappa legend

The `create_kappa_legend_gt()` function builds a small `gt` table that explains the color scale used by `kappa_fill()`, listing each agreement category with its color swatch and kappa range, plus a row for kappas that could not be estimated. It accompanies the kappa tables in the results pages, posters, and slides.

```{r}
#| label: fn-kappa-legend
#| eval: false
```

## Function to create heatmap

The `make_llm_agreement_heatmap()` function creates a paper-by-variable heatmap showing how many of the three language models matched the human-reviewed label for each observation. It can optionally relabel variables using `label_list`, reorder rows and columns by average agreement, hide paper IDs and adjust the left margin, and customize the plot title and subtitle. This figure is used to visualize where model agreement was high, where it was mixed, and which variables were most difficult for the models to classify consistently.

```{r}
#| label: fn-heatmap
#| eval: false
```
